This petition Under section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of .15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2.

The brief facts of the petitioner case are as under:
On 25.03.2023 at about 1.45 p.m., petitioner was getting down from the school van and while crossing the road cautiously near Ayyappa Swamy Temple, on Shanthinagar to K.G. Srikantapura road at Gangondanahalli, the Bajaj Pulsar Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ-8381 was ridden by the 1st respondent from Lakshmipura side at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to impact, petitioner fell down on the road and sustained severe bleeding injuries on his head, hands and legs and he became unconscious.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted Sparsh Hospital,
Goraguntepalya by the school van driver and thereafter he was shifted to Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health, South Hospital, Dharmaram College Post,
Bengaluru.

entities.text:
Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health, South Hospital, Dharmaram College Post,
Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In the said hospital X-ray and Scan was done to the petitioner, he has undergone surgery and took treatment as an inpatient from 25.03.2023 to 28.03.2023 and spent Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
The doctors have advised him to take follow up treatment regularly in future, for which he has to incur huge expenses.
3. It is further submitted that, prior to the accident petitioner was hale and healthy.
Due to accidental injuries, he has sustained permanent disability and lost his hopes, dreams, ambitions and his future became dark.

The jurisdictional Madanayakanahalli police have registered the case in Crime No.172/2023 and filed charge sheet for the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC Vishal M vs Chandrashekhar H S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141922692/
2 against the respondent No.1 for causing the accident.

sentences.text: The 1st respondent being the RC owner of the bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ-8381, which caused the accident and the 2nd respondent being the insurer and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Thus, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, petitioner has prayed to award compensation.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

5. Respondent No.1 has filed objection and contended that, the 2nd respondent company has issued the insurance policy vide No.0408033122P110212453 with effect from 11.01.2023 to 10.01.2024 in respect of Bajaj Auto Ltd/Pulsar 150 bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ-8381 after he was paying premium.
The compensation if any awarded by this Tribunal should be indemnified and paid by the insurance company.
This respondent has denied the injuries, treatment taken and amount spent by the petitioner towards treatment and disability sustained by him.
This respondent has admitted that, he is the R.C. owner of bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ- 8381 and he is having valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle at the time of accident.
It is contended that, the police have filed the false case against this respondent.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and exaggerated.

For all these reasons, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
6.
The respondent No.2/insurance company has filed objection and contending that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
This respondent has denied the issuance of insurance policy and its force with respect to vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ-8381 at the time of accident.
This respondent has denied the date, time and place of accident, injuries sustained, treatment taken in the hospital, disability suffered and the medical expenses incurred by him.

The specific contention of 2nd respondent is that, the alleged accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was crossing the road without observing the vehicle movement on the road and dashed to unknown vehicle.
Further, the false complaint was lodged against the rider of offending vehicle.
The delay in lodging the complaint itself indicates the said facts.
The petitioner has mainly contributed negligence to the accident.
The person who was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident had no valid driving license and the vehicle documents such as FC is not updated.

It is contended that, the police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6)
of M.V. Act.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner is simple and the compensation claimed by him is highly exorbitant and excessive.
For all these reasons, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed:-

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 25.03.2023 at about 1.45 p.m., when the minor petitioner was crossing the road after getting down the school van near Ayyappaswami Temple, K.G. Shrikantapura,Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru District, at that time, one Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ- Vishal M vs Chandrashekhar H S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141922692/
3 8381 came at high speed and hit the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Due to the impact, petitioner fell on the road,
sustained severe injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?

2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition? If so, from which respondent?
3. What Order or Award?
8. In order to prove the claim, the father of minor petitioner namely Sri. Manjunatha A., examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
Respondents No.1 and 2 have not adduced any evidence.
9. Heard on both side and perused the material on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 have filed written arguments.

10. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 11. ISSUE No.1:- In order to prove his claim, the father of minor petitioner is examined as PW.1 by way of filing affidavit evidence.
In his evidence, P.W.1 has reiterated the petition averments.

In support of his claim and also to prove Issue No.1, P.W.1 has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, copy of complaint at Ex.P.2, copy of final report at Ex.P,3, copy of spot panchanama at Ex.P.4, copy of MVA report at Ex.P.5, copy of victim statement at Ex.P.6, copy of statement of eye witness at Ex.P.7, copy of wound certificate at Ex.P.8, copy of reply to notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act at Ex.P.9 and copy of notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act at Ex.P.12.
Though, PW1 was cross examined at length, but his evidence was not shaken.

12. On the other hand, it is the contention of Respondent No.2 that, the alleged accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner, who was crossing the road without observing the vehicle movement on the road and dashed to unknown vehicle.
Further, the false complaint was lodged against the rider of offending vehicle.
The delay in lodging the complaint itself indicates the said facts.
The petitioner has mainly contributed negligence to the accident.
In order to prove the said contentions, respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral evidence and also not produced any documentary evidence.

Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove the actionable negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ-8381.
13.

From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of Ex.P.2 i.e., the complaint from the school van driver namely Divakar K.B., the Madanayakanahalli PS have registered the case as per Ex.P.1-FIR in Crime No.172/2023 for the offenses punishable U/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

4 due investigation the police have filed charge-sheet as per Ex.P.3 against the rider of Motor Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-04- EZ-8381 for the offenses punishable U/Sec. 279 and 338 of IPC.

sentences.text: As per Ex.P.4, the police have conducted spot panchaname.
As per Ex.P.5, the accident was occurred not due to any mechanical defect of the offending vehicle.
Ex . P.6
and Ex
. P.7 are the statements of petitioner and eye witness.
Ex.P.8 is the wound certificate and it shows that, the petitioner has sustained injuries due to road traffic accident.
As per Ex.P.9, the police have issued notice to the R.C. owner of offending vehicle and as per Ex.P.12, the R.C. owner of said vehicle has given reply.
Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has detailed cross examined PW.1, but he has failed to elicit anything from his mouth to disbelieve his version.

14. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same"
15. Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner and the evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code
. This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that due to actionable negligence on the part of the rider of Bajaj Pulsar Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.04-EZ-8381 the accident was occurred and the petitioner has sustained injuries.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE No.2:-
In view of discussion made while answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the minor petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount of Rs.2,87,393/- spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and nourishment and attendant charges.
17. It is relevant to note that the age of minor petitioner is shown as 11 years as on the date of accident.
In this regard PW-1 has produced Ex.P.10 the copy of Aadhar card of petitioner.

As per this Vishal M vs Chandrashekhar H S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141922692/
5 document the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 21.05.2012 and the accident was occurred on 25.03.2023.

entities.text: Vishal M vs Chandrashekhar H S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it is clear that as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 11 years.
18. In the instant case the petitioner has not examined doctor to prove the degree of his disability.
As already stated supra, absolutely there is nothing on record to show the extent of disability of petitioner caused due to accident.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to that effect, this Tribunal is not inclined to accept the version of the petitioner that he is having permanent disability caused in the accident.
19. The petitioner has not examined the doctor and there is not produced the disability certificate.

As per guidelines issued by the Central Government for the purpose of assessing the extent of specified disability in a person included under the rights of persons with disability Act 2016 dated 04-01-2018, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not come under the any disability.
Therefore, the injuries sustained by the petitioner do not cause any disability for the petitioner's body or part of the body.
However, in view of the injury sustained by him in the accident he had suffered pain.
20. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Petitioner has sought for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in road traffic accident.

P.W.1 has produced the medicals bills as per Ex.P.14 i.e., the bills at Serial No.1 to 29 amounting to Rs.1,83,755/- ( Inpatient bill of Rs.1,28,000/- + 55,755.26/- pharmacy bills ) to show the expenses incurred by him.
21. The natural guardian/father of minor petitioner has contended that due to accident his son has sustained injuries to his head, hands and legs.

In order to prove the injuries caused to petitioner,
P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.8 wound certificate.

On perusal of Ex.P.8 it is clear that the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1) Severe head injury with posterior right Cerebral EDH.
2) Left frontotemporal SDH 3) Bilateral SAH.
4) Fracture of right-Parieto-Occipital region.
5) Diffuse axonal injury.
The doctor opines that all the injuries are grievous in nature and he has sustained head injuries and fracture injury.
Further, P.W.1 has produced C.T. Scan report at Ex.P.13.
There are no evidences that the Petitioner is suffering from any difficulties which would affect his livelihood and day-today activities and earning capacity.
In the absence of medical evidence to prove disability, I deem it proper to award global compensation.

By considering the nature of injuries, age of the petitioner,
treatment taken in the hospital as stated supra and considering the pain and sufferings by the Vishal M vs Chandrashekhar H S on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141922692/

sentences.text: Petitioner, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.3,50,000/- as global compensation under all the conventional heads with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

22. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
23. The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner of Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ-8381 and Respondent No.2 is the insurer.
Hence, both the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to the compensation to the Petitioner.
The primary liability is on the Respondent No.2 to pay the compensation of Rs.3,50,000/- with 6% interest to the petitioner from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
24. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 3,50,000/- (Rupees Three lakhs fifty thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, the respondent No.2 being insurer of offending motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04-EZ-8381 is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two month from the date of this order.

After the deposit of compensation amount, since the petitioner is minor, but the minor guardian, who is the father of minor petitioner was expenses the medicals and other expenses, hence the 50% amount shall be released in the name of minor guardian of petitioner and 50% compensation amount shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank/scheduled bank till he attains the age of majority.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
